question: Which historical modules were actually present in modules_live, reached ONLINE, completed successfully, or failed at runtime?

observed_behavior: on accepted boot creates asyncio task janus_live_<module> and adds module to active_services
stores modules_live:last_boot with loaded count and active_services
stores modules_live:success:<module> on successful task completion in the recovered hardened lineage

searches_performed: Library semantic/exact searches for LIVE MODULE ONLINE, LIVE MODULE REWARDED, modules_live:success, modules_live:error and modules_live:last_boot
name-targeted searches for mod_rex, mod_auditor, mod_technoviking, mod_salo, mod_indus, hephaestus and memory_graph_service_prism
repeated searches excluding Python source files to suppress implementation-template matches
historical pc_local index search for literal modules_live directory paths

results.important_note: The root J\mod_*.py index proves file presence in the indexed J tree only; it must not be promoted to LIVE_DIRECTORY_FILE_PRESENCE.

allowed: MIGRATION_SELECTED when EXODUS selection evidence exists

claim_boundary.reason: Runtime receipts may survive only on authorized desktop/NAS backups, old janus.db files, deleted logs, private snapshots, or other sources not available in the current Library/index surface.
